items.goal: In src/WebApp/Components/Pages/Cart/CartPage.razor, handle a quantity that fails to bind or is out of range: do not call Basket.SetQuantityAsync, reload the items, render the item's saved quantity and unchanged totals, and show 'Enter a smaller quantity.' next to that item only. The message clears after a valid apply. Add a minimal scoped style in CartPage.razor.css only if needed, reusing existing message styles where they exist.
items.modelReason: Small fix, but the SSR form binding has subtle cases.
items.verifyReason: The bug and the fix are visible in the browser cart page.

alternatives.option: Change UpdateQuantityValue to long or string
alternatives.reason: Wider type still needs a range check; validating a null or invalid binding is simpler and also covers other non-numeric input.

alternatives.option: Clamp the value client-side with max on the input
alternatives.reason: Does not protect the server render; a posted large value would still blank the page.

items.reason: Small fix, but the SSR form binding has subtle cases.

subject: test-planner
reason: Split the bug into the regression check for valid quantity 2, the reproduction with 5000000000 (page stays and the message shows), unchanged quantity and totals including after a reload, the message clearing after a valid quantity, and the message staying on its own row when two items are in the bag; all e2e on the test stack as bob.

excluded.reason: Not defined by the ticket, only by the implementation notes (see Open questions)

excluded.item: Negative, zero, decimal or non-numeric typed quantities
excluded.reason: Undefined by the story (see Open questions)
Only in the implementation notes; the ticket does not describe it (see Open questions)
The fix is in the WebApp page; the API contract is unchanged
The ticket's contract is the page users see, which the e2e cases cover

items.title: Typing 2 and pressing Enter updates the item quantity and the bag totals
covers: Expected: Quantities that work today (for example 2) still work the same way
items.reason: The ticket requires that valid quantities keep working after the fix; the fix adds a validity check in front of the basket update, so a regression could reject or ignore valid values. It runs on e2e because the behaviour is the WebApp's enhanced form post on `/cart`.

items.title: Typing 5000000000 and pressing Enter keeps the bag page with header, item, totals and shows "Enter a smaller quantity."
covers: Expected: page stays on screen with header, items and totals
Expected: message 'Enter a smaller quantity.' next to the item
Actual: empty page must not happen
Steps to Reproduce 1-3
items.reason: This is the bug's exact reproduction: the value does not fit the quantity type and the page went blank with no message. It checks the page stays rendered and the shopper is told why; it is separate from TC-BUG-46-03, which checks the quantity and totals are unchanged. e2e because the failure was in the Blazor page's rendering after the form post.

items.title: After a too-large quantity, the item quantity stays 1 and the totals are unchanged, also after a reload
covers: Expected: item quantity stays what it was before (1)
Expected: bag totals unchanged
items.reason: The ticket requires the rejected value to change nothing: neither the displayed quantity and totals nor the stored basket. A partial fix could show the message but still write the value, or show a huge total. The reload proves the basket itself was not updated. e2e because the basket is reached only through the WebApp's gRPC client on the test stack.

items.title: The message disappears once a valid quantity is applied after a too-large one
covers: Expected: the message goes away once a valid quantity is applied
items.reason: The ticket states the message must go away after a valid quantity is applied; a stale message would tell the shopper their valid value was rejected. It needs the too-large post first, so it is its own case. e2e because the message is page state across two enhanced form posts.

items.title: With two items in the bag, the message appears only next to the item with the too-large quantity
covers: Expected: message shown next to that item
Expected: bag totals unchanged
items.reason: The ticket places the message "next to that item"; with more than one item a fix that shows it on every row, or on the wrong row, would mislead the shopper. The other item's quantity must also stay untouched. e2e because the per-row rendering is in the WebApp page.
